v0.1.0 quick reference card: raylib · raymath · rlgl

raymath: vectors are tuples, matrices are 16 numbers →

# Utils math


(clamp value min max) → number                                                # Clamp float value


(lerp start end amount) → number                                              # Calculate linear interpolation between two floats


(normalize value start end) → number                                          # Normalize input value within input range


(remap value input-start input-end output-start output-end) → number          # Remap input value within input range to output range


(wrap value min max) → number                                                 # Wrap input value from min to max


(float-equals x y) → number                                                   # Check whether two given floats are almost equal




# Vector2 math


(vector2-zero) → [x y]                                                        # Vector with components value 0.0f


(vector2-one) → [x y]                                                         # Vector with components value 1.0f


(vector2-add v1 v2) → [x y]                                                   # Add two vectors (v1 + v2)


(vector2-add-value v add) → [x y]                                             # Add vector and float value


(vector2-subtract v1 v2) → [x y]                                              # Subtract two vectors (v1 - v2)


(vector2-subtract-value v sub) → [x y]                                        # Subtract vector by float value


(vector2-length v) → number                                                   # Calculate vector length


(vector2-length-sqr v) → number                                               # Calculate vector square length


(vector2-dot-product v1 v2) → number                                          # Calculate two vectors dot product


(vector2-distance v1 v2) → number                                             # Calculate distance between two vectors


(vector2-distance-sqr v1 v2) → number                                         # Calculate square distance between two vectors


(vector2-angle v1 v2) → number                                                # NOTE: Angle is calculated from origin point (0, 0)


(vector2-line-angle start end) → number                                       # Current implementation should be aligned with glm::angle


(vector2-scale v scale) → [x y]                                               # Scale vector (multiply by value)


(vector2-multiply v1 v2) → [x y]                                              # Multiply vector by vector


(vector2-negate v) → [x y]                                                    # Negate vector


(vector2-divide v1 v2) → [x y]                                                # Divide vector by vector


(vector2-normalize v) → [x y]                                                 # Normalize provided vector


(vector2-transform v mat) → [x y]                                             # Transforms a Vector2 by a given Matrix


(vector2-lerp v1 v2 amount) → [x y]                                           # Calculate linear interpolation between two vectors


(vector2-reflect v normal) → [x y]                                            # Calculate reflected vector to normal


(vector2-min v1 v2) → [x y]                                                   # Get min value for each pair of components


(vector2-max v1 v2) → [x y]                                                   # Get max value for each pair of components


(vector2-rotate v angle) → [x y]                                              # Rotate vector by angle


(vector2-move-towards v target max-distance) → [x y]                          # Move Vector towards target


(vector2-invert v) → [x y]                                                    # Invert the given vector


(vector2-clamp v min max) → [x y]                                             # min and max values specified by the given vectors


(vector2-clamp-value v min max) → [x y]                                       # Clamp the magnitude of the vector between two min and max values


(vector2-equals p q) → number                                                 # Check whether two given vectors are almost equal


(vector2-refract v n r) → [x y]                                               # to the refractive index of the medium on the other side of the surface

(vector3-distance v1 v2) → number                                             # Calculate distance between two vectors

(vector3-max v1 v2) → [x y z]                                                 # Get max value for each pair of components

(vector3-to-float-v v) → [3 numbers]                                          # Get Vector3 as float array


(vector3-invert v) → [x y z]                                                  # Invert the given vector


(vector3-clamp v min max) → [x y z]                                           # min and max values specified by the given vectors


(vector3-clamp-value v min max) → [x y z]                                     # Clamp the magnitude of the vector between two values


(vector3-equals p q) → number                                                 # Check whether two given vectors are almost equal


(vector3-refract v n r) → [x y z]                                             # to the refractive index of the medium on the other side of the surface

# Matrix math


(matrix-determinant mat) → number                                             # Compute matrix determinant


(matrix-trace mat) → number                                                   # Get the trace of the matrix (sum of the values along the diagonal)

(matrix-identity) → [16 numbers]                                              # Get identity matrix


(matrix-add left right) → [16 numbers]                                        # Add two matrices


(matrix-subtract left right) → [16 numbers]                                   # Subtract two matrices (left - right)


(matrix-multiply left right) → [16 numbers]                                   # NOTE: When multiplying matrices... the order matters!


(matrix-translate x y z) → [16 numbers]                                       # Get translation matrix


(matrix-rotate axis angle) → [16 numbers]                                     # NOTE: Angle should be provided in radians


(matrix-rotate-x angle) → [16 numbers]                                        # NOTE: Angle must be provided in radians


(matrix-rotate-y angle) → [16 numbers]                                        # NOTE: Angle must be provided in radians


(matrix-rotate-z angle) → [16 numbers]                                        # NOTE: Angle must be provided in radians


(matrix-rotate-xyz angle) → [16 numbers]                                      # NOTE: Angle must be provided in radians


(matrix-rotate-zyx angle) → [16 numbers]                                      # NOTE: Angle must be provided in radians


(matrix-scale x y z) → [16 numbers]                                           # Get scaling matrix


(matrix-frustum left right bottom top near-plane far-plane) → [16 numbers]    # Get perspective projection matrix


(matrix-perspective fov-y aspect near-plane far-plane) → [16 numbers]         # NOTE: Fovy angle must be provided in radians


(matrix-ortho left right bottom top near-plane far-plane) → [16 numbers]      # Get orthographic projection matrix


(matrix-look-at eye target up) → [16 numbers]                                 # Get camera look-at matrix (view matrix)


(matrix-to-float-v mat) → [16 numbers]                                        # Get float array of matrix data




# Quaternion math


(quaternion-add q1 q2) → [x y z w]                                            # Add two quaternions


(quaternion-add-value q add) → [x y z w]                                      # Add quaternion and float value


(quaternion-subtract q1 q2) → [x y z w]                                       # Subtract two quaternions


(quaternion-subtract-value q sub) → [x y z w]                                 # Subtract quaternion and float value


(quaternion-identity) → [x y z w]                                             # Get identity quaternion


(quaternion-length q) → number                                                # Computes the length of a quaternion


(quaternion-normalize q) → [x y z w]                                          # Normalize provided quaternion


(quaternion-invert q) → [x y z w]                                             # Invert provided quaternion


(quaternion-multiply q1 q2) → [x y z w]                                       # Calculate two quaternion multiplication


(quaternion-scale q mul) → [x y z w]                                          # Scale quaternion by float value


(quaternion-divide q1 q2) → [x y z w]                                         # Divide two quaternions


(quaternion-lerp q1 q2 amount) → [x y z w]                                    # Calculate linear interpolation between two quaternions


(quaternion-nlerp q1 q2 amount) → [x y z w]                                   # Calculate slerp-optimized interpolation between two quaternions


(quaternion-slerp q1 q2 amount) → [x y z w]                                   # Calculates spherical linear interpolation between two quaternions


(quaternion-cubic-hermite-spline q1 out-tangent1 q2 in-tangent2 t) → [x y z w]  # as described in the GLTF 2.0 specification: https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#interpolation-cubic


(quaternion-from-vector3-to-vector3 from to) → [x y z w]                      # Calculate quaternion based on the rotation from one vector to another


(quaternion-from-matrix mat) → [x y z w]                                      # Get a quaternion for a given rotation matrix


(quaternion-to-matrix q) → [16 numbers]                                       # Get a matrix for a given quaternion


(quaternion-from-axis-angle axis angle) → [x y z w]                           # NOTE: Angle must be provided in radians


(quaternion-to-axis-angle q) → [[x y z] number]                               # Get the rotation angle and axis for a given quaternion


(quaternion-from-euler pitch yaw roll) → [x y z w]                            # NOTE: Rotation order is ZYX


(quaternion-to-euler q) → [x y z]                                             # NOTE: Angles are returned in a Vector3 struct in radians


(quaternion-transform q mat) → [x y z w]                                      # Transform a quaternion given a transformation matrix


(quaternion-equals p q) → number                                              # Check whether two given quaternions are almost equal


(matrix-decompose mat) → [[x y z] [x y z w] [x y z]]                          # Decompose a transformation matrix into its rotational, translational and scaling components

values →

# Values crossing the boundary


(draw-circle-v [x y] r :red)                       # vectors and rectangles are tuples (arrays work too)


(matrix-translate 1 2 3) → [16 numbers]            # matrices are 16 numbers in raylib field order: m0 m4 m8 m12 m1 ... (row-major)


(clear-background [245 245 245])                   # colors: [r g b], [r g b a] with 0-255 integers, or a keyword


(update-camera-pro {:position [0 2 4] ...} m r z)  # plain structs are structs/tables with kebab keys; all fields required


(key-down? :space)                                 # enum parameters take member keywords or integers


(set-config-flags [:vsync-hint :msaa-4x-hint])     # flag enums also take a tuple of keywords (OR-ed)


(check-collision-lines a b c d) → [bool [x y]]     # C out-parameters are returned, after the result


(set camera (update-camera camera :orbital))       # in/out parameters come back updated; rebind them


(draw-line-strip [[0 0] [10 5]] :red)              # array + count parameters take one tuple; the count is implied


(load-file-data "f.bin") → buffer                  # C memory returned by Load* is copied into Janet and freed
